papers.title: Biosynthesis of vanillin glucoside in Escherichia coli.
papers.abstractText: Vanillin is one of the most widely used flavorings worldwide. In this study, a de novo biosynthetic pathway for vanillin glucoside was established in Escherichia coli, accumulating 2.9 g/L of vanillin equivalent directly from glucose.

papers.title: Construction of Engineered Escherichia coli for Vanillin Production From Glucose: Pathway Optimization.
papers.abstractText: Biotechnological production of natural vanilla substitutes avoids synthetic petrochemical routes. We constructed an engineered E. coli strain for the efficient production of vanillin directly from glucose by deleting endogenous aldehyde reductases.

papers.title: Discovery of a thermostable eugenol oxidase for vanillin biosynthesis from vanillyl alcohol.
papers.abstractText: Biocatalytic synthesis of flavor aldehydes requires resilient enzymes under harsh reaction conditions. The engineered enzyme enabled the biocatalytic synthesis of natural vanillin in high space-time yield with 99% conversion.

papers.title: Rational Engineering of Carboxylic Acid Reductase for Improved Vanillin Biosynthesis.
papers.abstractText: Carboxylic acid reductases reduce vanillic acid into vanillin during microbial bioconversion. The mutant carboxylic acid reductase exhibited a 4.2-fold increase in vanillin production compared to the wild-type enzyme.

papers.title: Biotransformation of ferulic acid to vanillin by Amycolatopsis sp.
papers.abstractText: Ferulic acid from agricultural byproducts is an ideal natural precursor for flavoring synthesis. Amycolatopsis strain ATCC 39116 converted ferulic acid into vanillin with a molar yield of 68% in fed-batch bioreactors.

papers.title: Catalytic oxidation of kraft lignin to vanillin using copper-based heterogeneous catalysts.
papers.abstractText: Valorization of lignin into fine chemicals is key to circular bioeconomy frameworks. We achieved catalytic depolymerization of industrial kraft lignin to yield pure vanillin with high selectivity under mild hydrothermal conditions.

papers.title: Microbial production of natural vanillin by metabolically engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum.
papers.abstractText: Corynebacterium glutamicum tolerates high aromatic concentrations, making it suitable for flavor synthesis. Corynebacterium glutamicum was metabolically engineered to biosynthesize vanillin from lignin-derived aromatics at industrial scale.

papers.title: One-pot chemoenzymatic synthesis of vanillin from eugenol.
papers.abstractText: Eugenol is an inexpensive natural allylbenzene extracted from clove oil. A two-step one-pot chemoenzymatic reaction was developed for the scalable synthesis of vanillin without hazardous organic solvents.

papers.abstractText: Green extraction technologies preserve heat-labile aroma components. Under optimized acoustic power, natural vanillin was extracted from cured pods with a yield of 2.45 g/100g dry weight within 30 min.
